chunks: So close your eyes, O creatures of Allāh, from its worries and engagements,
because you are sure about its separation and its changing conditions.
Fear it like a sincere fearer and one who struggles hard,
and take a lesson from what you have seen about the falling places of those before you,
namely that their joints were made to vanish, their eyes and ears were destroyed, their honour and prestige disappeared and their pleasure and wealth came to an end.
The nearness of their children changed into remoteness. The company of their spouses changed into separation with them.
They do not boast over each other, nor do they beget children nor meet each other nor live as neighbours.

key_terms.الْكَادِحِ: the hardworking / one who exerts effort

ai.seo_question: How should Muslims view the transient nature of worldly life according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) employs vivid imagery of the decay of past generations to illustrate the impermanence of worldly attachments, urging believers to adopt a stance of prudent detachment. This reflection aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere renunciation, but as a conscious awareness of the transient nature of *dunya* compared to the eternal *akhirah*. By comparing the world to a fleeting guest, the text encourages spiritual vigilance and preparation for the inevitable separation from kin, status, and pleasure.
